gloss: be left over, remain; leave over; abound, excel; remainder, excess, profit; cord
summary: To be over and above: what is left when the rest is gone, and what goes beyond the measure. The niphal is to be left or remain, Elijah “left, I alone” and the remnant left in Zion; the hiphil is to leave over (eat and leave over, 2Ki 4:43–44), to leave a remnant as Yahweh did, lest Israel be like Sodom (Isa 1:9, quoted in Rom 9:29), and to make abound. The nouns are the rest or remainder (יֶתֶר, above all “the rest of the acts” of the kings), the excess or pre-eminence beyond the measure, and in Ecclesiastes יִתְרוֹן, מוֹתָר and יוֹתֵר, the profit or advantage that is left to a man for his toil, of which he has none over the beast in death (Ecc 3:19). Akkadian watāru “exceed” and watru “surplus” share the sense. A second group, יֶתֶר and מֵיתָר “cord, bowstring, tent rope”, matches Arabic watar, Sabaean wtr and Syriac yatrā “bowstring, cord”; how the cord belongs with the excess is not shown.

words.gloss: be left over, remain; leave over, leave a remnant; make abound; excel
words.summary: About 110 times, in the niphal and the hiphil only. What is left is set against what is taken, eaten, burnt, cut off or killed: “two parts cut off … the third left” (Zec 13:8); “the upright will dwell in the land, the blameless remain in it, the wicked cut off from it” (Pro 2:21–22). The brief's tokens with no stem are the noun יוֹתֵר and the name הוֹתִיר filed by spelling.

stems.gloss: be left, remain over; (participle) the rest, the remainder; the remnant

senses.definition: Of a person, a thing or a group: to be left when the others are gone, killed or used up; often “left alone” or, negated, “not one was left”.

evidence.note: “וַיִּוָּתֵר יַעֲקֹב לְבַדּוֹ”: Jacob was left alone, the others having crossed over.
“His brother is dead, וַיִּוָּתֵר הוּא לְבַדּוֹ of his mother.”
“They have killed your prophets with the sword, וָאִוָּתֵר אֲנִי לְבַדִּי.” Quoted in Rom 11:3.
“אֲנִי נוֹתַרְתִּי a prophet of Yahweh, I alone; but the prophets of Baal are 450 men.”
The locusts ate what the hail had left (הוֹתִיר), “וְלֹא־נוֹתַר any green thing”.
“The waters covered their adversaries; not one of them נוֹתָר.”
“The daughter of Zion נוֹתְרָה like a booth in a vineyard.”
All in Hezekiah's house carried to Babylon: “לֹא־יִוָּתֵר a thing.” So 2Ki 20:17.
“If ten men יִוָּתְרוּ in one house, they shall die.”
“No Anakim נוֹתַר in the land … only in Gaza, Gath and Ashdod נִשְׁאָרוּ”: the two verbs side by side.
“I נוֹתַרְתִּי there beside the kings of Persia.”
The wall built “and no breach נוֹתַר in it”.
1Ki 19:10 quoted: “I alone am left (ὑπελείφθην).” Paul answers (11:4–5) that there is a remnant (λεῖμμα) chosen by grace.

senses.definition: The participle הַנּוֹתָר, הַנּוֹתָרִים: the rest of a group or the remainder of a thing, once a part is taken out: the rest of the flock, the remaining names, sons, cities or vessels; the remainder of an offering after Yahweh's part.

evidence.note: Six names on one stone “and the six הַנּוֹתָרִים on the second stone”.
Jacob tended “the rest (הַנּוֹתָרֹת) of Laban's flocks”.
After the memorial portion is burnt, “וְהַנּוֹתֶרֶת of the grain offering is for Aaron and his sons”.
Aaron's “remaining (הַנּוֹתָרִים) sons”, after Nadab and Abihu died; and “the grain offering הַנּוֹתֶרֶת”.
“You shall not leave (תוֹתִירוּ) any of it until morning, וְהַנֹּתָר of it until morning you shall burn.”
“הַנּוֹתָר of the flesh of the sacrifice on the third day shall be burnt with fire.”
“The rest (הַנּוֹתָרִים) of the sons of Kohath” received ten cities.
“The vessels הַנּוֹתָרִים in the house of Yahweh.”
The 5,000 “הַנּוֹתָר in the breadth”, common land for the city, beside the holy portion.
“הַנּוֹתָרִים fled to Aphek.”
“We have eaten and been satisfied and left over plenty … וְהַנּוֹתָר is this great store.”

senses.definition: Of a people after judgment: those left alive when the rest are cut off, to whom Yahweh's promise passes.

evidence.note: “He who is left (הַנִּשְׁאָר) in Zion and הַנּוֹתָר in Jerusalem will be called holy, everyone written for life in Jerusalem”: parallel to שָׁאַר.
“Two parts in it will be cut off and die, and the third יִוָּתֶר in it”: opposite כָּרַת.
“Everyone הַנּוֹתָר of all the nations that came against Jerusalem will go up year by year to worship the King, Yahweh of armies.”
“The upright will dwell in the land, and the blameless יִוָּתְרוּ in it; but the wicked will be cut off from the land.”
“Behold, survivors נוֹתְרָה in it, sons and daughters brought out.”
“Everyone הַנּוֹתָר in the midst of the land will eat curds and honey.”
“Till you are left like a pole on the top of a mountain.”
“Everyone הַנּוֹתָר in your house” (Eli's) will come begging a priest's place.

stems.gloss: leave over; leave a remnant, spare; make abound, have more than enough; excel

senses.definition: To leave part of something when the rest is eaten, taken or destroyed: food left over after eating one's fill, the Passover and the manna that must not be kept until morning, chariots spared from the hamstringing.

evidence.note: Twenty loaves before a hundred men: “thus says Yahweh, אָכֹל וְהוֹתֵר”; “they ate, וַיּוֹתִרוּ, according to the word of Yahweh.”
“She ate and was satisfied, וַתֹּתַר”; and gave Naomi “what she had left over (הוֹתִרָה) after she was satisfied” (2:18).
Of the manna: “let no one leave (יוֹתֵר) any of it until morning”; some did (וַיּוֹתִרוּ), and it bred worms.
“You shall not leave any of it until morning.”
David hamstrung the chariot horses “but left (וַיּוֹתֵר) of them a hundred chariots”. So 1Ch 18:4.
“Those you leave (תּוֹתִירוּ) of them will be pricks in your eyes.”
“The rest of his children אֲשֶׁר יוֹתִיר.”

senses.definition: Of Yahweh: to leave some alive out of a judgment, so that a people is not wholly destroyed.

evidence.note: “Unless Yahweh of armies הוֹתִיר לָנוּ a survivor (שָׂרִיד), a few, we would have been like Sodom.”
Isa 1:9 quoted: “unless the Lord of armies had left us a seed”; the Peshitta writes אַותַּר, this root's verb.
“וְהוֹתַרְתִּי, when you have those who escape the sword among the nations.”
“I will leave a few men of them from the sword, famine and plague, that they may declare their abominations.”
“To cut off from you man and woman … so as to leave you no remnant (שְׁאֵרִית).”
“I gather them to their own land, וְלֹא־אוֹתִיר עוֹד any of them there”: none left among the nations.
“According to the greatness of your arm, הוֹתֵר the sons of death”: keep alive those appointed to die.

senses.gloss: make abound; have more than enough
senses.definition: To give more than is needed, so that there is a surplus; of Yahweh, to prosper a people with plenty.

evidence.note: “Yahweh וְהוֹתִרְךָ for good in the fruit of your womb, your cattle and your ground, on the land Yahweh swore to your fathers to give you.”
The same promise after the return: “Yahweh will again rejoice over you for good.”
The materials for the tabernacle “were sufficient for all the work, וְהוֹתֵר”: and more than enough.
“We have eaten and been satisfied and left over (וְהוֹתֵר) plenty, for Yahweh has blessed his people.”

senses.definition: To be over the others in rank: said of Reuben, the firstborn, who loses it.

evidence.note: After “יֶתֶר of dignity and יֶתֶר of power” (49:3): “unstable as water, אַל־תּוֹתַר, because you went up to your father's bed.”
“Unless the Lord of Sabaoth had left (ἐγκατέλιπεν) us a seed”: Isa 1:9.
“I alone am left (ὑπελείφθην)”: 1Ki 19:10.

parallels.note: “Remain, be left”: set beside it of the same remnant.
The upright dwell in the land, the blameless remain in it.

opposites.note: “Be cut off”: what is cut off against what is left.
What is eaten against what is left over.

words.summary: About ninety times, most often in the construct “the rest of”: the rest of the people, of the acts of a king. Less often it is what is over the measure: pre-eminence, abundance, “exceedingly”. The brief counts the cord יֶתֶר and the name Jether with it, by spelling.

senses.definition: The rest of a group or thing, beside the part already named.

evidence.note: Two thousand with Saul, a thousand with Jonathan, “וְיֶתֶר הָעָם he sent away”.
“Half of it I burned in the fire … וְיִתְרוֹ shall I make an abomination?”
In the seventh year the poor eat, “וְיִתְרָם the beast of the field shall eat”.
“יֶתֶר of the cutting locust the swarming locust ate”, three times over.
“וְיֶתֶר דִּבְרֵי Rehoboam … are they not written in the book?”: the formula closing a king's reign, some forty times in Kings and Chronicles.
“Only Og king of Bashan was left מִיֶּתֶר הָרְפָאִים.”
“יֶתֶר הָעָם left in the city … Nebuzaradan carried away.” So Jer 39:9; 52:15.
Hezekiah: “I am deprived of יֶתֶר שְׁנוֹתָי”, the rest of my years, at the gates of the grave.
“Until she who is in labour has borne, וְיֶתֶר אֶחָיו will return to the sons of Israel.”
“Half of the city will go into exile, וְיֶתֶר הָעָם will not be cut off from the city.”
“The remnant (שְׁאֵרִית) of my people will plunder them, וְיֶתֶר גּוֹיִי will possess them”: parallel to שְׁאֵרִית.
“All יֶתֶר עַמִּים will plunder you.”
“And the rest of the tribes”: Benjamin, Simeon, Issachar, Zebulun, Gad.

senses.definition: What is over and above: rank beyond the others, speech beyond what fits, greatness beyond measure; with a verb, “exceedingly”.

evidence.note: Reuben, “my firstborn, my strength … יֶתֶר שְׂאֵת וְיֶתֶר עָז”: excelling in dignity and power; lost in 49:4, “אַל־תּוֹתַר”.
“שְׂפַת־יֶתֶר is not fitting for a fool; how much less lying lips for a noble”: lofty, excessive speech.
The drunkards: “tomorrow will be as this day, גָּדוֹל יֶתֶר מְאֹד”, great beyond measure.
The little horn “וַתִּגְדַּל־יֶתֶר toward the south, the east and the beautiful land”.
“Yahweh keeps the faithful, and repays עַל־יֶתֶר the one who acts proudly”: in full, beyond measure.

senses.definition: A man's surplus or wealth, what he has more than he needs.

evidence.note: Men of the world, “their portion in this life … they leave יִתְרָם to their children”.
“Fire has consumed יִתְרָם”, of the wicked.

evidence.locator: יֶתֶר → λοιποί ×6, κατάλοιπος ×2 (brief's counts, homographs together)

words.summary: A cord: green cords that bind Samson, the string of a bow, the cord of a tent. Its tokens are filed by spelling with the noun “remainder”, so the counted uses are those of יֶתֶר as a whole; the cord is only Jdg 16:7–9, Psa 11:2, Job 4:21 and Job 30:11. Arabic, Sabaean and Syriac have the same word for bowstring and cord; how “cord” relates to “be over” is not shown by any verse.

senses.definition: A cord or string: of fresh gut or sinew to bind with, the string of a bow, the cord that holds a tent.

evidence.note: “If they bind me with seven יְתָרִים לַחִים that have not been dried”; Samson snapped them “as a thread of tow snaps when it touches fire”.
“The wicked bend the bow, they have set their arrow עַל־יֶתֶר to shoot at the upright.”
Men “who dwell in houses of clay” (4:19): “is not יִתְרָם pulled up (נִסַּע, the word for striking a tent) in them? They die, and not in wisdom.”
“He has loosed יִתְרִי (ketiv יתרו) and afflicted me”: the slackened cord or bowstring.

senses.definition: The ropes that stretch out and hold a tent or the hangings of the court; once, the strings of a bow.

evidence.note: “The pegs of the tabernacle, the pegs of the court, וּמֵיתְרֵיהֶם.”
The hangings of the court “וּמֵיתָרָיו”, in the Gershonites' charge; the court's pillars, pegs and cords in the Merarites' (3:37; 4:32).
To barren Zion: “Enlarge the place of your tent … הַאֲרִיכִי מֵיתָרַיִךְ and strengthen your pegs.”
“My tent is destroyed, and all מֵיתָרַי are broken; my children have gone from me.”
“בְּמֵיתָרֶיךָ you will aim at their faces”: on your bowstrings.

words.summary: Only in Ecclesiastes, ten times: what is left over to a man as gain for his toil under the sun, and the advantage one thing has over another.

senses.definition: What a man has over and above, as the return for his labour; the Preacher's question is whether any remains under the sun.

evidence.note: “מַה־יִּתְרוֹן to man for all his toil that he toils under the sun?”
“All was vapour and striving after wind, and there was no יִתְרוֹן under the sun.”
“As he came, so shall he go; and what יִּתְרוֹן has he who toils for the wind?”
“וְיִתְרוֹן of a land is in all.”

senses.definition: The advantage one thing has over another, with מִן “over”.

evidence.note: “There is יִתְרוֹן to wisdom over folly, as יִתְרוֹן of light over darkness.”
“וְיִתְרוֹן of knowledge: wisdom preserves the life of him who has it.”
“If the iron is blunt … וְיִתְרוֹן הַכְשֵׁר is wisdom.”
“If the serpent bites before it is charmed, there is no יִתְרוֹן to the charmer.”
“Those who receive the abundance (περισσείαν) of grace … will reign in life.”

words.summary: A participle-form noun, eight or nine times, in Ecclesiastes and Esther and once in Samuel: what is over, the advantage, and as an adverb “more, besides, too much”. 1Sa 15:15 הַיּוֹתֵר “the rest” and Exo 16:19 יוֹתֵר are filed under the verb as well, by spelling.

senses.definition: What is over to a man, the gain or advantage.

evidence.note: “מַה־יּוֹתֵר to the wise over the fool?”
“Many words increase vapour; מַה־יֹּתֵר to man?”
“Wisdom is good with an inheritance, וְיֹתֵר to those who see the sun.”

senses.definition: As an adverb: more than, in addition; or beyond what is fitting.

evidence.note: Haman: “whom would the king delight to honour יוֹתֵר מִמֶּנִּי?”
“וְיֹתֵר מֵהֵמָּה, my son, be warned: of making many books there is no end.”
“וְיֹתֵר, besides being wise, the Preacher taught the people knowledge.”
“Do not be over-righteous, and do not make yourself יוֹתֵר wise.”
“Why then was I אָז יוֹתֵר wise?”
“וְאֶת־הַיּוֹתֵר we devoted”: the rest, after sparing the best.

senses.definition: Gain that comes from toil, opposite to want; and the advantage of one over another.

evidence.note: “In all toil there is מוֹתָר, but the talk of lips is only to want (מַחְסוֹר).”
“The plans of the diligent are only לְמוֹתָר, but everyone who is hasty only to want.”
“As one dies so dies the other; they all have one breath, וּמוֹתַר הָאָדָם מִן־הַבְּהֵמָה אָיִן.”

senses.gloss: abundance, what one has laid by
senses.definition: The wealth a people has gained and stored up, carried off or lost in flight.

evidence.note: Moab: “יִתְרָה they have made and their store (פְּקֻדָּתָם) they carry over the brook of the willows.”
“יִתְרַת עָשָׂה has perished.”

words.gloss: lobe (of the liver), the appendage over the liver
words.summary: Eleven times, always of sacrifice: “הַיֹּתֶרֶת עַל־הַכָּבֵד”, burnt on the altar with the fat and the kidneys. The form is the feminine participle “that which is over”, the part standing out over the liver. No cognate gives the word, so its tie to the root rests on the form alone.

senses.gloss: lobe or appendage over the liver
senses.definition: A part of the liver of a sacrificial animal, named as “over” or “from” the liver, taken off with the kidneys and burnt with the fat as Yahweh's portion.

evidence.note: “All the fat that covers the entrails, וְאֵת הַיֹּתֶרֶת עַל־הַכָּבֵד, and the two kidneys … burn them on the altar.”
“הַיֹּתֶרֶת עַל־הַכָּבֵד, with the kidneys he shall remove it.”
“הַיֹּתֶרֶת מִן־הַכָּבֵד of the sin offering.”

words.summary: Daniel's Aramaic, eight times: of Daniel's “excellent spirit”, and of the brightness of the image, the heat of the furnace and the terror of the fourth beast, all beyond the ordinary.

senses.definition: Above the measure of others: the spirit, knowledge and wisdom found in Daniel, the greatness added to Nebuchadnezzar.

evidence.note: “רוּחַ יַתִּירָה and knowledge and understanding … were found in Daniel.”
Daniel was distinguished above the presidents and satraps “because רוּחַ יַתִּירָא was in him”.
“Light and understanding and וְחָכְמָה יַתִּירָה are found in you.”
Restored to his kingdom, “וּרְבוּ יַתִּירָה was added to me”.

senses.definition: Of a quality beyond the usual: bright, hot, strong, dreadful.

evidence.note: The image: “its brightness יַתִּיר stood before you, and its appearance was terrible”.
“The furnace was heated יַתִּירָא”, so that the flame killed those who took up the three.
The fourth beast “dreadful and terrible and strong יַתִּירָא”.
“Dreadful יַתִּירָה, its teeth of iron and its claws of bronze.”

words.gloss: remain over; abound, gain; leave over; excel
words.summary: The Peshitta's verb for what remains over (Greek περισσεύω): the fragments left when the multitudes had eaten, as in Elisha's feeding (2Ki 4:43–44); for leaving a remnant in Rom 9:29, where it renders Isa 1:9 with this root's own verb; and for abounding, gaining and excelling.

senses.definition: To be left over when all have eaten their fill.

evidence.note: “When they were satisfied: gather the fragments דִּיתַֿרו, that nothing be lost.”
Twelve baskets of fragments “דִּיתַֿרו to those who had eaten”.

senses.definition: To be more than another, or to gain more.

evidence.note: “Unless your righteousness תִּאתַֿר more than the scribes and Pharisees, you will not enter the kingdom of heaven.”
“What will a man profit if he נִאתַֿר the whole world and loses his life?”

senses.definition: To leave a part when the rest is eaten; of the Lord, to leave survivors.

evidence.note: Isa 1:9: “unless the Lord of armies אַותַּר לַנ a survivor, we would have been as Sodom.”
“They took up the fragments מֵדֵּמ דַּאותַּרו, twelve baskets.”

stems.gloss: abound, have more than enough; be better off

senses.definition: To have more than enough, or grow beyond measure.

evidence.note: “To him who has will be given, וְנֵתֿיַתַּר לֵה.”
“Where sin increased, there grace אֵתֿיַתּרַתֿ.”
“That your love may increase and abound in knowledge.”
“If we eat, we are not the better (מֵתֿיַתּרִינַנ); if we do not eat, the worse.”

senses.definition: The participle מיַתַּר: to be above another in worth.

evidence.note: The birds are fed: “are you not מיַתּרִינ more than they?”
The Son made greater than the angels, “as the name he inherited דַּמיַתַּר over theirs”.

senses.definition: More than or greater than another, with מֵנ “than”; what is over and beyond.

evidence.note: “A prophet? Yes, and יַתִּיר מֵנ a prophet.”
“Behold, one יַתִּיר than Solomon is here.”
“Let your word be yes, yes, no, no; what is יַתִּיר than these is from evil.”
“How much יַתִּיר is a man than a sheep.”
To love God and one's neighbour “is יַתִּירָא than all burnt offerings and sacrifices”.

senses.definition: What one gains; the advantage a thing gives.

evidence.note: “To me to live is the Messiah, and if I die it is יֻותֿרָנָא.”
“What was יֻותֿרָנָא to me I counted loss (חֻוסרָנָא) for the Messiah.”
“What then is the superiority of the Jew, or what is יֻותֿרָנָה of circumcision?”
Foolish questions: “there is no יֻותֿרָנ in them.”
The former commandment set aside “for its weakness and because there was no profit in it”.

senses.definition: The remainder left over from the feeding of the multitudes; and the overflow of the heart.

evidence.note: “They ate and were satisfied, and took up תַּותָּרֵא of the fragments, twelve baskets full.”
“Out of תַּותָּרַי of the heart the mouth speaks.” So Luk 6:45.

cognates.gloss: exceed, be(come) outsize, do to excess; (watru) additional, surplus, excellent; (watartu) excess
cognates.note: The verb and its adjective and noun carry both halves of the Hebrew: what is over (surplus, additional) and what surpasses (excellent, outstanding), as יֶתֶר does in Gen 49:3 and Aramaic יַתִּיר in Daniel. Akkadian initial w answers to Hebrew initial י, as in watāru beside יָתַר.

evidence.note: “augment; be(come) greater; exceed; do something to excess; make surpassing.”
“additional; excellent; excess; extra; greater; more; outstanding; surpassing; surplus.”
“addition; excess.”
“profit; superfluity”: compare מוֹתָר and יִתְרוֹן.

evidence.locator: SEM000530 wtr [excess] V, AKK014559 watāru, ARM012217 YTR [remain], HEB003243 yatar

cognates.gloss: remain over, abound, gain, excel; yattīrā more, greater; yūṯrānā profit; tawtārā remainder
cognates.note: The Syriac root has all the Hebrew senses but the cord: what remains over, abundance, gain and profit, excelling. Its words are entry words above where the Peshitta uses them.

evidence.locator: lexeme 1445, ;TR (root 858 ;TR), gain; remain over; abound; make abound; prefer; benefit
lexemes 1441 ;OTRNA, lucre, advantage, profit, gain, abundance; 1442 ;T;RA, more, excessive, greater, better, excelling; 1449 TOTRA, remainder

cognates.gloss: bowstring, string; (verb) brace the string of a bow
cognates.note: The same word as the cord יֶתֶר and מֵיתָר, of the bowstring above all (Psa 11:2; 21:13). Arabic initial w answers to Hebrew initial י. Arabic has no sense “remain over” or “excess” in this root.

evidence.locator: Book I, p. 2918, art. وتر, وَتَرٌ (n41601)

cognates.note: The Arabic root's other main sense: one over, unpaired. It could be “one left over” beside the Hebrew “remain over”, but no Arabic use joins it to excess or remainder, so it is not named on any word.

doctrine.statement: Isaiah says that unless Yahweh had left (הוֹתִיר) Israel a few survivors, they would have been like Sodom and Gomorrah, wholly destroyed (Isa 1:9). Paul quotes the verse of Israel in his own day (Rom 9:29), and answers Elijah's “I alone am left” (1Ki 19:10) with the seven thousand Yahweh had kept, “so now there is a remnant chosen by grace” (Rom 11:3–5). Those left in Zion are called holy, “written for life in Jerusalem” (Isa 4:3), and Yahweh keeps some of the scattered alive among the nations (Ezk 6:8). So the remnant is not left by its own strength: Yahweh leaves it, and it is the line through which his promises go on.

Yahweh promised to make Israel abound (הוֹתִיר) “on the land that Yahweh swore to your fathers to give you” (Deu 28:11), and again after he has gathered them from the nations (Deu 30:3–5, 9). Ezekiel says that when he gathers them to their own land he will leave (אוֹתִיר) none of them among the nations any more (Ezk 39:28). Proverbs says the upright will dwell in the land and the blameless remain (יִוָּתְרוּ) in it, while the wicked are cut off from it (Pro 2:21–22). So the promise is of a real land and a real people gathered into it, with none left behind; and only the blameless remain there.

Zechariah sees all the nations gathered against Jerusalem; half the city goes into exile, but the rest of the people (יֶתֶר הָעָם) is not cut off (Zec 14:2). Then Yahweh goes out to fight, his feet stand on the Mount of Olives, and he is king over all the earth (Zec 14:3–4, 9). Everyone left (הַנּוֹתָר) of those nations then goes up to Jerusalem year by year to worship the King, Yahweh of armies, and to keep the feast of סֻכּוֹת (Zec 14:16). So the kingdom is on earth, with Jerusalem as its centre and survivors of the nations living under it.

The Preacher asks what profit (יִתְרוֹן) is left to man under the sun (Ecc 1:3), and says of death that man has no advantage (מוֹתַר) over the beast: as one dies so dies the other, they all have one breath (רוּחַ), all go to one place, all are from the dust and all return to the dust (Ecc 3:19–20). Eliphaz speaks of men who dwell in houses of clay, whose foundation is in the dust: their cord (יִתְרָם) is pulled up like a tent's, and they die (Job 4:19–21). So scripture does not give man, in death, anything the beast lacks: no part of him lives on, and his hope is not in his nature but in God, who will raise the dead (Dan 12:2).

note: Drafted 2026-11-18. Root key יתר as the brief and BDB key it; no other entry used the root's keys (tur.json has j.ef.ab, a cross-reference to תּוּר, and keeps it). BDB keys assigned: j.ef.aa verb, j.ef.ac יֶתֶר “remainder”, j.ef.ad יֶתֶר “cord”, j.ef.al יִתְרוֹן, j.ef.aj יוֹתֵר, j.ef.ao מוֹתָר, j.ef.ag יִתְרָה, j.ef.ap מֵיתָר, j.ef.ak יֹתֶרֶת, xj.an.ab Aramaic יַתִּיר. Names in their own files: names/jether.json (j.ef.ae יֶתֶר, j.ef.af יִתְרָא), names/jethro.json (j.ef.ah), names/ithran.json (j.ef.am), names/ithream.json (j.ef.ar), names/hothir.json (j.ef.an), names/abiathar.json (a.ae.bc, which BDB files under אבה). Left out: j.ef.ai the gentilic יִתְרִי “the Ithrite” (Ira and Gareb, 2Sa 23:38; the clan of Kiriath-jearim, 1Ch 2:53), j.ef.aq the town יַתִּיר Jattir (Jos 15:48; 21:14; 1Sa 30:27; 1Ch 6:42), j.ef.as יְתֵת Jetheth (Gen 36:40), whose spelling lacks the ר and whose root is not shown, and the zero-token cross-references e.bd.ab, m.be.ae, m.bw.aj. Shared tokens: j.ef.ac, j.ef.ad and j.ef.ae all count the same 108 tokens of the spelling יֶתֶר, so the cord's counted uses are not its own (it is Jdg 16:7–9; Psa 11:2; Job 4:21; 30:11 only; Job 30:11 is a ketiv יתרו and may not be tokenized under any key); the verb's key counts יוֹתֵר (Ecc 2:15; 6:8; 7:16; Est 6:6) and הוֹתִיר (1Ch 25:4) by spelling, and j.ef.an counts three hiphil verbs (Exo 10:15; Isa 1:9; Jer 44:7). Job 4:21 is read as the tent cord (נִסַּע is the striking of a tent) rather than “their excellence”; Job 22:20 is read as “their abundance”. Sounds: the root has none of the merged letters (י ת ר), so no sounds are recorded; whether “cord” and “be over” are one root cannot be decided by a merger. The cord's cognates (Arabic watar, Sabaean wtr, Syriac yatrā, which Wiktionary files under ܘܬܪ) have no sense of excess, and the excess cognates (Akkadian watāru, Syriac ytr) have no cord; open question whether these are two older roots *wtr in one spelling. Arabic witr “single, odd” is recorded as possible and named on no word. Not consulted: Payne Smith and Brockelmann for the Syriac yatrā (cited from Wiktionary only); SabaWeb or Biella for Sabaean wtr (Wiktionary only); CAL for Targumic יְתַר and יַתִּיר; CAD for watāru; Ge'ez (Anderson–Moser's geez wtr “attentive” does not match and is not recorded; a Ge'ez “bowstring” is a lead from other lexicons, not followed). Peshitta: the words are SEDRA root 858 (;TR); verse lists from BFBS.TXT through tblWords (lexeme 1445 verb 80 tokens, 1442 יַתִּירָא 100, 1443 the adverb יַתִּירָאִיתֿ 78, not entered, 1441 יֻותֿרָנָא 12, 1449 תַּותָּרָא 5, 1444 יַתִּירֻותָֿא “abundance” 7, 1446 מַותּרָנָא, 1447 מְיַתּרָא, 1448 מְיַתּרֻותָֿא, not entered). The Syriac verb's stems are assigned from the vocalized forms (peal תִּאתַֿר, aphel אַותַּר, ethpaal נֵתֿיַתַּר, pael participle מיַתַּר) and should be checked. Greek: Septuagint renderings kept only as the bridge; σκληρός (Gen 49:3) and φαρέτρα (Psa 11:2) not recorded. Open questions: (1) the yotheret's identity (lobe, caudate process) is not fixed by scripture; (2) Pro 17:7 שְׂפַת־יֶתֶר “excessive” or “excellent” speech; (3) Psa 31:24 עַל־יֶתֶר “in full” or “exceedingly”; (4) the doctrine statements are reasoned conclusions to review.
